title: Sanitize legacy flag graph, archive ghost rollouts, and remove admin-proxy compatibility shim
creator: Lena Park
description: Background: Over years of iterative rollout features we've accumulated a tangled flag DAG, stale admin-proxy shims, and a set of 'ghost' rollout records that increase config load time and confuse operators. This ticket aims to safely collapse the legacy flag graph, archive or compact old rollout history into an immutable archive store, and remove the compatibility shim used by the old admin proxy that surfaces v0/v1 route variants. Goal: reduce config parsing latency, simplify rollout evaluation logic, and eliminate a maintenance burden while preserving the ability to debug historical state.
acceptance_criteria: All legacy admin-proxy compatibility code paths removed from runtime routing layer
Rollout history older than 18 months is migrated to archived store and is no longer loaded into the live config manifest
Flag dependency graph trimmed so that active namespace evaluation path depth is reduced by >= 30% in p95 load tests
No user-facing changes for customers on Dedicated or Hosted APIs after canary; verified via smoke tests and customer integration suites
Rollback path documented: a one-click restore from archived store to live manifest within 30 minutes
Relevant dashboards updated to show: archive migration progress, config load times pre/post change, and any failed rollout reconciliations
rollout_plan: 1) Create read-only snapshot of current rollout manifests and flag graph; store in S3/archival bucket. 2) Run the offline compactor to identify ghost rollouts and unreferenced flag nodes (staging). 3) Create a feature-flagged canary build that disables admin-proxy shim for 5% of traffic in the staging cluster. 4) Monitor for 48 hours: config-load latency, rollout-eval errors, KPI regressions. 5) Increment canary to 30% then 100% if metrics are green. 6) Run migration job to move eligible history to archive and update manifest generator to exclude archived items. 7) Deploy runtime removal patch for compat shim and prune the old route translation table. 8) Post-mortem and update runbook.
migration_steps: Generate immutable snapshot and checksum of current manifest (S3://redwood-archives/flags/manifest-2025-02-28)
Run 'flag-graph-compact' job in staging with 1x traffic and verbose logging
Open a short-lived admin console view showing candidate nodes to remove for manual approval
Schedule archive batch job during off-peak window (UTC 02:00-05:00)
Deploy canary removing compat shim behind feature flag and watch tracing for any 5xx correlated to route resolution
Once canary passes, run full migration and deploy removal; keep hot-rollback mechanism that re-inserts shim from archived blob
notes: Trade-offs: keeping full historical rollouts live simplifies some debugging stories but adds runtime overhead. We opted to archive >18mo by default while leaving a fast-restore path for extenuating customer investigations. Open question: should we expose an 'expanded history' mode in Console for enterprise customers? Engineering review recommended deferring that to a follow-up PM ticket.
